mainTopic: Found תפילין on שבת, knots and bows, checking תפילין bought from an unproven seller, and the משנה's rules for bundles and danger
overview: This amud deals with תפילין. It opens with the end of a ברייתא about תפילין found outside on שבת: רבי מאיר lets the finder bring in new or old ones by wearing them, while רבי יהודה allows only old ones. The גמרא first reads the dispute as a question of whether people make amulets that look like תפילין. A teaching of אבוה דשמואל בר רב יצחק then shows that 'new' means real תפילין whose straps are not yet knotted, so the real issue is tying a knot on שבת. On the question 'why not tie a bow?', רב חסדא says a bow is invalid for תפילין, and אביי says רבי יהודה holds a bow counts as a full knot. Next, רב rules that someone buying תפילין from an unproven seller checks three, from both the arm and head kinds, and the גמרא connects this to how many times it takes to set a חזקה, including the view of רבי and the special case of bundles. Finally, the גמרא explains the משנה's terms צבתים and כריכות, when one brings found תפילין in pair by pair or waits until dark, and how the rule in a time of danger depends on whether the danger comes from גוים or from bandits.

steps.title: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה on new and old tefillin
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a dispute. רבי מאיר says found תפילין may be brought in whether they are new or old. רבי יהודה forbids new ones and permits old ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether new or old, these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה forbids new ones and permits old ones.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing a ברייתא about finding תפילין outside on שבת. רבי מאיר says you may bring in any תפילין by wearing them, while רבי יהודה allows only old ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is that you rescue the תפילין by wearing them, because wearing תפילין does not count as carrying. רבי מאיר makes no distinction between new and old. רבי יהודה treats new תפילין differently, and the next steps will try to explain why.

phrases.english: whether new ones or old ones,
phrases.notes: Still the ברייתא: the finder may bring in either kind.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda forbids new ones
and permits old ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד חֲדָשׁוֹת וְאֶחָד יְשָׁנוֹת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: found תפילין, new or old, may be brought in. רבי יהודה: only old ones may be.

steps.title: Inference that the תנאים disagree about whether a person bothers to make a fake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the dispute is about whether a person goes to the trouble of making an amulet that looks like תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It seems that one master holds a person does bother, and the other master holds a person does not bother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the ברייתא. It says the two תנאים disagree about whether people bother to make an amulet shaped like תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds טרח איניש, meaning people do make such amulets, so a new pair might really be an amulet and not תפילין. Old pairs have clearly been worn as תפילין. רבי מאיר holds people do not bother, so anything that looks like תפילין really is תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: A person goes to the trouble (here, to make an amulet that looks like תפילין)

phrases.english: Apparently, one master holds a person goes to the trouble,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה, so new תפילין might be amulets.

phrases.english: and one master holds a person does not go to the trouble.
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר, so anything shaped like תפילין is תפילין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a principle out of the ברייתא's dispute.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of whether a person makes fake amulets that look like תפילין is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's split between new and old tefillin

steps.title: Redefining new and old: everyone agrees no one makes fakes
steps.stepSummary: A teaching defines 'old' תפילין as those whose straps are already knotted and 'new' as those whose straps are not knotted. The dispute is therefore not about fakes, and everyone holds people do not bother to make them.
steps.simpleTranslation: (A memory aid.) Now that the father of שמואל בר רב יצחק taught that old tefillin are those with straps that are knotted, and new ones have straps that are not knotted, it turns out that everyone agrees a person does not bother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the inference from the previous step. A new definition of 'new' and 'old' shows that both sides agree nobody makes fake תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'New' does not mean possibly fake. It means real תפילין whose knots have not been tied yet. Tying a permanent knot is forbidden on שבת, so new תפילין cannot be worn normally. That is why רבי יהודה forbids bringing them in, and it has nothing to do with amulets.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid (mnemonic) for the statements that follow

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'new' תפילין are suspected fakes. In this reading they are real תפילין whose straps simply have not been knotted yet.
steps.whyThisMatters: It moves the whole dispute away from the question of fakes. The issue is now the שבת problem of tying knots, which sets up the next question about tying a bow.

phrases.english: (Shin-yod-tzadi-yod ayin-tzadi-beit-yod is a mnemonic.)
phrases.notes: A memory aid for the upcoming statements. It is not part of the argument.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּתָנֵי אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: And now that the father of Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak has taught:
These are the old ones —
any that have straps and are knotted,

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָשׁוֹת — יֵשׁ בָּהֶן רְצוּעוֹת וְלֹא מְקוּשָּׁרוֹת.
phrases.english: new ones — they have straps but are not knotted.
So everyone agrees that a person does not go to the trouble.
phrases.notes: The dispute now depends on whether the knot is already tied.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּתָנֵי אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 2 by redefining the terms of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the תנאים disagree about טרח איניש
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed 'new' meant possibly fake. In fact 'new' means real תפילין that are not yet knotted.

steps.title: Why not just tie a bow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה's ruling: he could tie the straps of new תפילין with a bow, which is not a permanent knot, and wear them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him just tie them with a bow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יהודה's reason for forbidding new תפילין. It suggests he could tie a temporary bow instead of a real knot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a permanent knot is forbidden on שבת. If a bow is allowed on שבת and works for תפילין, the new pair could be worn and brought in. So why does רבי יהודה forbid it?

keyTerms.meaning: A bow (a loop knot that is easy to untie)
Let him tie them with a bow

phrases.english: But let him simply tie them with a bow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new explanation of רבי יהודה given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ban on bringing in new (unknotted) תפילין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bow avoids the forbidden permanent knot and would let him wear the tefillin, so there seems to be no reason to forbid it.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a bow is invalid for tefillin
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא learns from here that a bow does not work for תפילין. A real knot is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This teaches that a bow is invalid for tefillin.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the challenge. Tying a bow would not help, because תפילין tied with a bow are not valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bow may be allowed on שבת, but it does not make the תפילין wearable as a מצוה. Without a valid knot he cannot wear them, so he cannot bring them in. The phrase זאת אומרת shows that רב חסדא is drawing a new הלכה out of רבי יהודה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: תפילין, the boxes worn on the arm and head

steps.whyThisMatters: It yields a practical הלכה: תפילין tied with a bow instead of a real knot are not valid.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
That is to say,
a bow is invalid for tefillin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a hidden הלכה that blocks the suggested solution
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bow would solve the problem, since it is allowed on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: A bow does not make תפילין valid, so it does not help.

steps.title: אביי: for רבי יהודה a bow counts as a real knot
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a different answer. רבי יהודה holds elsewhere that a bow is a full knot, so tying it on שבת is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי יהודה follows his own view, for he said that a bow is a full-fledged knot.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the same challenge another way. The bow is not the solution, because for רבי יהודה tying a bow on שבת is like tying a real knot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's problem was that the תפילין would be invalid. אביי's problem is that the bow itself is forbidden on שבת. In אביי's reading, a bow might be valid for תפילין, but רבי יהודה still does not allow tying it on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to 'why not tie a bow?'. רב חסדא says a bow is invalid for תפילין. אביי says that, for רבי יהודה, a bow is a real knot and is forbidden on שבת.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
for he said: a bow is a full-fledged knot.
phrases.notes: So tying a bow on שבת is forbidden in his view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than רב חסדא to the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Connects the ruling to the תנא's known position elsewhere (לטעמיה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bow is a temporary loop and is allowed on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, a bow counts as a real knot and is forbidden on שבת. This does not prove that a bow is invalid for תפילין.

steps.title: How could a bow be good enough for תפילין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: his answer assumes a bow would work for תפילין, but the knot of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני with a set shape.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason a bow is forbidden is that a bow counts as a full knot. If it were not, one could tie the תפילין with a bow. But didn't רב יהודה son of רב שמואל בר שילת say in the name of רב: the knot of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני? And רב נחמן added: its decorative side must face outward!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer from Step 6. It shows that the knot of תפילין has a special required form, so a simple bow should not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי explained that רבי יהודה forbids tying a bow on שבת only because a bow counts as a real knot. That suggests that, without the שבת problem, a bow would work for תפילין. But the knot of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני with a fixed shape, and רב נחמן says its decorated side must face out, so a loose bow seems unacceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: A bow, a loop knot that can be pulled open easily
A law given orally to משה at סיני, not written in the תורה
The special knot of the תפילין straps

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question about רבי יהודה's ruling. It targets אביי's answer from Step 6, which seemed to say a bow would be fine for תפילין.

phrases.english: The reason is that a bow is a full knot,
phrases.notes: Restating אביי's reasoning from Step 6

phrases.english: so if that were not so, he could tie them with a bow,
phrases.notes: This is the idea the גמרא is about to challenge.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
phrases.english: But didn't רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת, say
phrases.notes: וְהָאָמַר tells you a challenge is coming from a teaching we already know.

phrases.english: in the name of רב:

phrases.aramaic: קֶשֶׁר שֶׁל תְּפִילִּין הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי הוּא,
phrases.english: The knot of תפילין is a law given to Moshe at Sinai,
and רב נחמן said: and their decorative side faces outward!
phrases.notes: The knot has a set form and a front side, so it seems to require a real knot

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of אביי's answer in Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's implication that a bow would be valid for תפילין if not for the שבת issue
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The knot of תפילין is a הלכה למשה מסיני with a fixed form and a decorated front, so a simple bow should not qualify

steps.title: The bow is tied in the shape of the real knot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we are talking about a bow tied to look exactly like the required תפילין knot.
steps.simpleTranslation: He ties them with a bow shaped like their proper knot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי. The bow in question is tied in the same shape as the special תפילין knot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה למשה מסיני requires a certain shape, and a bow can be made in that shape. So the bow meets the shape requirement without being a permanent knot. אביי's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, in the form of
He ties them with a bow

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, a bow tied in the shape of the תפילין knot works for תפילין. רבי יהודה forbids it on שבת only because he holds a bow counts as a real knot.

phrases.english: It is where he ties them with a bow
in the form of their proper knot.
phrases.notes: The bow copies the required shape

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the bow is tied in the required shape
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bow is a loose loop and cannot match the set form of the תפילין knot
steps.terutzMaskana: A bow can be tied in the shape of the תפילין knot, which satisfies the הלכה למשה מסיני

steps.title: Checking תפילין bought from someone who is not a proven expert
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא in the name of רב: a buyer of תפילין from a non-expert checks two of one kind and one of the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רב: One who buys תפילין from someone who is not a proven expert checks two arm-תפילין and one head-תפילין, or two head-תפילין and one arm-תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב חסדא, quoting רב, rules how many pieces a buyer must check when buying a batch of תפילין from an unproven seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking three pieces shows whether the seller is reliable. If all three are kosher, the seller gains a חזקה and the rest of the batch can be trusted. The ruling mixes kinds: two of one and one of the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A proven expert, someone shown to be reliable

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base ruling the גמרא is about to question. The question will be why the buyer checks a mix of kinds instead of three of the same kind.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Rav said:
One who buys tefillin from someone who is not an expert,

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹדֵק שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁל יָד וְאַחַת שֶׁל רֹאשׁ,
phrases.english: checks two of the arm and one of the head,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁל רֹאשׁ וְאַחַת שֶׁל יָד.
phrases.english: or two of the head and one of the arm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about buying תפילין, still within the larger subject of תפילין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer from a non-expert checks three pieces: two of one kind and one of the other

steps.title: If bought from one person, he should check three of the same kind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a 'whichever way you look at it' challenge. If everything came from one seller, he should check three of one kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if he is buying from one man, let him check either three arm-תפילין or three head-תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to challenge רב's ruling with a two-sided argument. This passage gives only the first side; the second side comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה is set by three instances. If one person made or supplied all the תפילין, checking any three pieces of the same kind should be enough, so why mix kinds? The second side of the מה נפשך, about buying from more than one source, follows in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it; a two-sided challenge
Three, the number that sets a חזקה

steps.confusionAlert: A מה נפשך has two sides. This step gives only the first side ('if from one man'). Step 11 gives the second side, so do not treat the challenge as finished here.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it:
phrases.notes: Opens a two-sided challenge

phrases.english: if he is buying from one man,
phrases.notes: First side of the dilemma

phrases.english: let him check either three of the arm
or three of the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's requirement to check a mix of two of one kind and one of the other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all came from one source, three checks of any single kind should set a חזקה, so mixing kinds seems unnecessary. The second side of the dilemma continues next.

steps.title: The other side: if he bought from several sellers, every pair needs checking
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the 'whichever way' challenge. If the תפילין came from two or three different sellers, then every single one should need checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he bought them from two or three different people, then each and every one should need to be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the two-sided challenge it started in step 10. This is the second side: if the buyer bought from several sellers, checking only three is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seller earns trust only for his own work. If the תפילין came from different people, checking one seller's pair says nothing about another seller's pair. So רב's 'two plus one' fails either way: one seller means 'three of one kind,' and many sellers means 'check them all.'

phrases.english: If he bought from two or three people,
each and every one should require checking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second side of the two-sided challenge begun in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא in the name of רב: check two of one kind and one of the other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With many sellers, each seller must be tested on his own work. Checking just three tests nobody fully, so every pair would need checking.

steps.title: One seller, who must prove himself on both kinds
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he really bought everything from one seller. The seller has to show expertise in both the של יד and the של ראש, so both kinds must be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he bought from one man. But we need the seller to prove he is an expert in both the hand-תפילין and the head-תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by choosing the 'one seller' side. It explains why רב did not say 'three of one kind.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a של יד (one compartment) is a different skill from making a של ראש (four compartments). Proving skill in one kind does not prove skill in the other, so the check must include both kinds. That gives three total, split between the two kinds.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (used to set out the true case)
That he proves himself an expert

phrases.english: Really, he bought from one man,
and we require that he prove himself an expert
in the arm-תפילין and in the head-תפילין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided challenge of steps 10-11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case (one seller) and adds a reason (expertise in both kinds).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With one seller, three of any kind should be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: With one seller, his skill must be shown in both kinds. So the three checked must include both של יד and של ראש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the reason behind רב's mixed count, and that reason drives the rest of the sugya.

steps.title: רבה בר שמואל's ברייתא seems to say three of one kind
steps.stepSummary: A challenge from a ברייתא of רבה בר שמואל: 'one checks three, of the arm and of the head.' The גמרא suggests this means three of the arm or three of the head, which would go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבה בר שמואל taught: with תפילין, one checks three of the arm and of the head. Doesn't that mean either three arm-תפילין or three head-תפילין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given by quoting a ברייתא. It also offers a reading of that ברייתא which seems to contradict רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said both kinds must be checked. The ברייתא says 'three,' and the גמרא suggests it means three of a single kind, all arm or all head. If so, checking one kind would be enough, which goes against רב's rule and against step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that…? (suggests a reading to prove a point)

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But רבה בר שמואל taught:

phrases.aramaic: בִּתְפִילִּין בּוֹדֵק שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁל יָד וְשֶׁל רֹאשׁ,
phrases.english: with תפילין, one checks three of the arm and of the head,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו אוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁל יָד
phrases.english: is it not either three of the arm
or three of the head!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא תָּנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 12 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the seller must be checked on both kinds (step 12, and רב's ruling).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא means three of a single kind, then one kind is enough, and the mixed requirement falls.

steps.title: No: three total, some arm and some head
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that reading. The ברייתא means three in total, made up of both kinds, which fits רב exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means three in total: some of them arm-תפילין and some of them head-תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the challenge by rereading the ברייתא. Read correctly, the ברייתא supports רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'of the arm and of the head' describe what the three are made of. They do not mean three of each, or three of only one kind. So the ברייתא matches רב's 'two of one kind and one of the other.'
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'three of the arm and of the head' as three of each (six total). It means three altogether, mixed between the two kinds.

phrases.english: No:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ, מֵהֶן שֶׁל יָד מֵהֶן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ.
phrases.english: three, some of them of the arm and some of them of the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא: שָׁלֹשׁ, מֵהֶן שֶׁל יָד מֵהֶן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'מאי לאו' reading of step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the suggested reading of the ברייתא. The ברייתא itself stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenger assumed the three were all of one kind. The text can just as well mean three mixed between the kinds.

steps.title: רב כהנא's ברייתא says only two
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge: רב כהנא taught that one checks two, of the arm and of the head. That is fewer than רב's three.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב כהנא taught: with תפילין, one checks two, of the arm and of the head!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that clashes with רב on the number. Here the number itself is different, so it cannot be fixed by rereading the words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב requires three checks in total. רב כהנא's ברייתא says two, so the conflict is about how many checks build trust in the seller.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (opens a challenge from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: But רב כהנא taught:

phrases.aramaic: בִּתְפִילִּין בּוֹדֵק שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁל יָד וְשֶׁל רֹאשׁ!
phrases.english: with תפילין, one checks two, of the arm and of the head!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first ברייתא was settled, a second ברייתא is raised against רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא requires only two checks, which contradicts the number three.

steps.title: That ברייתא follows רבי: a חזקה comes after two times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב כהנא's ברייתא follows רבי, who holds that a חזקה is set after two times. רב follows the view that it takes three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי, who said that a חזקה is set by two times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the clash by tying the ברייתא to a different תנא. The two numbers come from a known disagreement about how a חזקה is formed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking the seller's work is really about building a חזקה, a settled assumption that he is reliable. Most views need three times to set a חזקה. רבי needs only two. So two checks follows רבי, and three checks (רב) follows the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: A settled assumption, built by something happening repeatedly

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the number of תפילין to check rests on the wider rule of how many times it takes to set a חזקה.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is רבי,
who said: by two times it becomes a חזקה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the ברייתא to a different תנא (מאן תנא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב כהנא's ברייתא disagrees with רב on the same principle.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי (two times make a חזקה). רב follows the view that three are needed.

steps.title: But the same ברייתא mentions a third bundle
steps.stepSummary: A challenge to the answer: the end of רב כהנא's ברייתא says to check the second bundle and the third bundle. רבי would not need a third check.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי, look at the end of that ברייתא: 'and likewise the second bundle, and likewise the third bundle.' If it is רבי, does he hold of a third?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 16 using the end of the very same ברייתא. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said the ברייתא follows רבי, for whom two times are enough. But the end of the ברייתא requires checking a third bundle, which fits the three-times view. So it seems the ברייתא cannot follow רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Look at (say) the end of that teaching

phrases.english: If it is רבי, say the end of the ברייתא:
and likewise with the second bundle,
and likewise with the third bundle.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי רַבִּי — שְׁלִישִׁי מִי אִית לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And if it is רבי, does he hold of a third?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 16 using the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב כהנא's ברייתא follows רבי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי sets a חזקה after two times, so he needs no third check. Yet the end of the ברייתא requires a third bundle, so it does not seem to follow רבי.

steps.title: רבי agrees that bundles come from different sellers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 17. רבי agrees that bundles need a third check, because bundles of תפילין are bought from two or three different people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי agrees about bundles, because people buy them from two or three different men.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of why רבי's ברייתא checks a third bundle. In the special case of bundles, רבי agrees that two good bundles do not prove anything about the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה after two times works only when the items share one source. Bundles are usually bought from different makers. So two good bundles say nothing about a bundle from a different maker, and the third must be checked too.

keyTerms.meaning: agrees, concedes (even though his general view is different)

phrases.english: Rabbi concedes regarding bundles,
phrases.notes: Even though רבי usually says two times make a חזקה.

phrases.english: because one buys them from two or three different people.
phrases.notes: Different makers mean no shared quality.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 17 that רבי would not need a third check.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction: bundles are a special case where רבי's two-time חזקה does not apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי would always stop checking after two items.
steps.terutzMaskana: For bundles bought from different sellers, even רבי requires a third check.

steps.title: Then the fourth and fifth should need checking too
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is that bundles come from different people, then the fourth and fifth bundles should also need checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even the fourth should need checking too, and even the fifth too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If bundles come from different makers, why stop at three? Every bundle should need to be checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic of 'different sellers' does not stop at any number. So the ברייתא's mention of only a second and a third bundle now looks too limited.

phrases.english: If so,
even the fourth also should be checked,
and even the fifth also!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning that bundles come from different sellers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If each bundle may come from a different maker, then every bundle needs checking. So why does the ברייתא mention only up to the third?

steps.title: Yes, all bundles are checked; 'third' only blocks a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the fourth and fifth bundles must also be checked. The ברייתא mentions the third only to show that no חזקה is formed after two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so. The reason it teaches 'third' is to exclude a presumption. Really, even the fourth and fifth also must be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge. Every bundle must be checked. The ברייתא said 'third' only to teach that two good bundles do not create a חזקה here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'third' is not a limit. It is a signal that רבי's usual two-time rule does not apply to bundles. Once that is clear, every further bundle obviously needs checking as well.
steps.whatToRemember: With bundles of תפילין, every bundle is checked. Even רבי agrees that no חזקה forms, because the bundles come from different makers.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Third' here is not a maximum. It only shows that the two-time חזקה is cancelled for bundles.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.
And this that it teaches 'third'
is to take it out of its presumptive status,
phrases.notes: Two good bundles do not make a חזקה here.

phrases.english: but really, even the fourth and fifth must be checked as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge in Step 19 and reinterprets the word 'third' in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenge and reinterpreting the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Third' seemed to mean that one checks only up to three bundles.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Third' only cancels the חזקה. In fact all bundles are checked.

steps.title: What are צבתים and כריכות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's phrase 'found them in צבתים or כריכות' and asks what each word means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If he found them in bundles or wrapped piles, etc.' What are bundles, and what are wrapped piles?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. It asks for the meaning of two terms used there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses two different words for groups of found תפילין. The גמרא wants to know whether they describe different things and how they differ.

phrases.english: 'If he found them in bundles or wrapped piles, etc.'
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: What are bundles, and what are wrapped piles?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the checking discussion back to explaining words in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definitions of צבתים and כריכות.

steps.title: Both are multiple pairs, arranged differently
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says both terms mean many pairs of תפילין. צבתים are arranged in pairs, while כריכות are many wrapped together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: These are bundles, and these same ones are wrapped piles. Bundles are arranged pair by pair. Wrapped piles are many wrapped together.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains that both words describe many תפילין found together. The difference is only in how they are arranged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In צבתים, each head תפילה is tied with an arm תפילה as a pair. In כריכות, many are wrapped together with no pairing. Both cases involve more תפילין than one could easily wear in at once.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
these are bundles,
and these same ones are wrapped piles.
phrases.notes: Both mean many pairs together.

phrases.english: Bundles: arranged in pairs,
wrapped piles: many wrapped together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב הֵן הֵן צְבָתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both are groups of many תפילין. צבתים are tied in pairs, and כריכות are many wrapped together.

steps.title: Why wait until dark? Bring them in pair by pair!
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says one waits with them until dark. The גמרא asks why he cannot simply wear them in one pair at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'He waits with them until dark and then brings them.' But why? Let him bring them in pair by pair!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling and challenges it. Bringing them in pair by pair, the normal method for found תפילין, seems possible here too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a few found תפילין, the rule is to wear them in one pair at a time, which is allowed on שבת. Since צבתים are already arranged in pairs, the same method should work. So why should he sit and wait?

phrases.english: 'He waits with them until dark and brings them.'
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: And why?
Let him bring them in pair by pair!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next ruling of the משנה about bundles.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling to wait until dark with bundles.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pair-by-pair carrying works for a few תפילין. So it should work here too, and waiting should not be needed.

steps.title: Pair by pair only if he can finish before sunset
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק son of רב יהודה reports his father's explanation. If he can finish bringing them in pair by pair before sunset, he does so. If not, he waits with them until dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק son of רב יהודה said: It was explained to me by my father. Whenever, if he brings them in pair by pair, he would finish before sunset, he brings them in pair by pair. And if not, he waits with them until dark and brings them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's 'wait until dark' is for a large amount. With fewer תפילין, he really does bring them in pair by pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is time. If all pairs can be brought in before sunset, he uses the pair-by-pair method. If there are too many, he could not finish anyway, so he guards them and brings them all after שבת ends.

keyTerms.meaning: it was explained to me personally

steps.whatToRemember: Found תפילין are brought in pair by pair if this can be finished before sunset. If not, one waits with them until dark.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical test, whether he can finish before sunset, for choosing between the two methods in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehuda said:
it was explained to me personally
by my father,
any case where, if he brings them in pair by pair,
they would be finished before sunset,
he brings them in pair by pair.
And if not,
he waits with them until dark and brings them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the משנה's ruling applies only when there are too many to finish before sunset.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to require waiting with any bundle.
steps.terutzMaskana: He waits only when bringing them in pair by pair cannot be finished before sunset.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's rule for a time of danger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: in a time of danger, the finder covers the תפילין and goes on his way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And in a time of danger, he covers them and goes on his way.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up the next move, where a ברייתא will seem to disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the משנה taught that the finder normally waits with the תפילין until dark, or wears them in pairs. This line adds an exception: when there is danger, he does not wait. He covers the תפילין where they lie and goes on his way, leaving them there.

keyTerms.meaning: And he walks on / goes on his way

phrases.english: And in a time of danger, he covers them and goes on his way.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה; the next question is about these words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the clause about waiting until dark, the גמרא moves to the משנה's next clause, which covers a time of danger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a time of danger, the finder of תפילין covers them and continues on his way.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives a different rule for danger
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that in danger the finder carries the תפילין less than four אמות at a time. This seems to contradict the משנה's 'cover them and go.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: 'And in a time of danger, he carries them less than four אמות at a time'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא that seems to give a different instruction for the same situation of danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה tells him to cover the תפילין where they are and walk away without them. The ברייתא instead has him take them along in short stages, each less than four אמות. Moving in short stages avoids the full איסור of carrying four אמות in a רשות הרבים. So the two sources disagree about how to handle danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Each time less than four אמות, moving in short stages

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying he may carry the תפילין normally. 'Less than four אמות at a time' means stopping before each four אמות. This way he never does the full act, forbidden by the תורה, of carrying four אמות in a רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: 'And in a time of danger'
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא starts a challenge from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: he carries them less than four cubits at a time!
phrases.notes: This conflicts with the משנה's 'cover them and go.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's rule for danger just quoted in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that in danger one covers the תפילין and goes on his way.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא describing the same case of danger gives a different method: carrying in stages of less than four אמות. Both cannot be the rule for the same situation.

steps.title: Two kinds of danger: gentiles versus bandits
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the משנה speaks of danger from גוים, and the ברייתא speaks of danger from ליסטים (bandits).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: This is not difficult. This source (the משנה) is speaking about danger from גוים. That source (the ברייתא) is speaking about danger from bandits.
steps.whatsHappening: רב resolves the contradiction by saying the two sources describe different dangers, so each one has its own rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With danger from גוים, the government has banned תפילין, so being seen with them is the danger itself. He therefore covers them where they are and leaves without them. With danger from bandits, the only danger is staying in place until dark, and having the תפילין with him is not the problem. So he can take them with him, moving them less than four אמות at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. Introduces a resolution.
Danger from gentile authorities who decreed against תפילין

steps.whatToRemember: The kind of danger decides the method. If the תפילין themselves are the danger (a government decree), he covers them in place and walks away without them. If only staying in place is dangerous (bandits), he takes them along in short stages of less than four אמות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: when two sources seem to clash, the גמרא often finds that each one describes a different real-life situation.

phrases.english: Rav said: It is not difficult:
phrases.notes: 'It is not difficult' is the usual way of starting an answer.

phrases.english: this (the Mishnah) is in a case of danger from gentiles,
phrases.notes: Being seen with תפילין is dangerous, so he covers them where they are and leaves without them.

phrases.english: that (the Baraita) is in a case of danger from bandits.
phrases.notes: Only staying put is dangerous, so he may move the תפילין in short stages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different type of danger.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא both describe the same danger and give conflicting rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to danger from gentile authorities, where the תפילין must be hidden. The ברייתא refers to danger from bandits, where he may move the תפילין less than four אמות at a time.
